injects.title: Last-minute polling place relocation
injects.scene: It is 7:20 a.m. The building you were going to open at has been shut to the public, and the site has to move. Voters are already in the parking lot.

atk.where: For example: the main downtown polling place, a community center where about 900 people vote.
atk.what: For example: the building is locked without warning, and staff and voters are left in the parking lot.
atk.when: For example: 6:45 a.m., before opening, so there is no time to reroute.
atk.goal: For example: long lines at the backup site, and a story that the county can't run a clean election.

injects.op: Secure a new site, move equipment and supplies, staff it, sign the old door, maintain chain of custody in transit.
injects.comms: Voters, poll workers and the call center all need the new address within minutes. Mapping tools and AI assistants will keep serving the old address for hours no matter what you post.
injects.prec: Routine nationally. In Ridgewood, N.J., a threat closed a school on Election Day 2025 and voters had to be redirected mid-day.

ai.task: Build the rumor that beats the county's notice. Use a chatbot to write three versions of the post that says the move was deliberate.
ai.prompt: Write three social media posts, under 40 words each, from a resident of a fictional county who believes their polling place was moved at the last minute to hold down turnout. Angry, specific, plausible, no profanity. Put EXERCISE MATERIAL at the top of each one.

injects.title: Evacuation from a threat or device
injects.scene: Police have cleared the building. Poll workers are on the sidewalk, voters are being turned away at the door, and nobody can say yet how long it will be.

atk.where: For example: a busy polling place in a shopping center next to a bus stop.
atk.what: For example: a suspicious package is reported, the building is cleared, and nobody is sure who can declare it safe.
atk.when: For example: mid-morning, when the line is longest, with the building closed for two hours.
atk.goal: For example: votes never cast, and a belief that the election was shut down.

injects.op: Keep voting going somewhere. Chain of custody for equipment left behind. Possible court-ordered hours extension.
injects.comms: Two facts on separate tracks: safety status and voting continuity. Voters need to know their ballot still counts.
injects.prec: An unknown explosive device was thrown from a vehicle near a Catasauqua, Pa., polling place during the May 2026 primary. No injuries, voting was not interrupted, and a nearby election director described keeping materials staged to deploy a pop-up site under a tent if needed.

ai.task: Write the alert that did not come from the election office. Use a chatbot to draft the forwarded text message that shuts the county down.
ai.prompt: Draft a two-sentence emergency text alert, written to sound official, telling recipients that voting has been suspended countywide after a police incident and that they should go home. Use a fictional county and a fictional agency. Put EXERCISE MATERIAL at the top.

injects.title: Weather or natural hazard closes or damages voting sites

sponsor.name: PEER
sponsor.full: Partnership for Elections and Emergency Response

injects.scene: The storm came through overnight. Some of your sites have water in them, some have no road access, and your staff are calling in about their own homes.

atk.where: For example: the low-lying east side of the jurisdiction, where three sites sit near the river.
atk.what: For example: flooding closes two sites and cuts the road to a third, and power is out at a backup location.
atk.when: For example: the night before Election Day, too late to move anything by the usual process.
atk.goal: For example: voters cut off from any open site, and poll workers who can't reach their sites.

injects.op: Damage assessment, relocation or consolidation, generators, road access for staff and equipment, resupply.
injects.comms: Voters need the new site and the reason in one message. Displaced voters may no longer be at the address on file, so the channels you normally rely on will not reach them.
injects.prec: Hurricanes Helene and Milton destroyed or closed polling sites across Florida and North Carolina before the 2024 general election. One Sarasota County voter was sent to three locations before finding the right one. Florida supervisors describe hurricane planning as a standing part of the 2026 cycle.

ai.task: Generate the image that arrives before your damage assessment does, then write the caption that travels with it.
ai.prompt: Generate a photo-realistic image of a small-town community center with flood water at the entrance and a half-submerged vote-here sign. Then write a 25-word caption claiming the county is hiding how many sites are underwater. Watermark the image EXERCISE MATERIAL.

injects.title: Power outage at a voting location
injects.scene: The lights go out at a busy site mid-morning. Tabulators are on battery, the line is not moving, and phones are already coming out.

atk.where: For example: a school gym polling place, with the whole block around it going dark.
atk.what: For example: a transformer fails, the lights and check-in laptops go down, and power isn't back for two hours.
atk.when: For example: the midday rush, when the most voters are waiting.
atk.goal: For example: slow down the line, and a story that the voting machines were tampered with.

injects.op: Battery backup on tabulators, generator, emergency ballot procedures, decision on whether to relocate.
injects.comms: Say the site is open and ballots are being counted. An outage reads as a closure unless you say otherwise.
injects.prec: A power outage affected two Maricopa County voting centers during the July 2026 primary and power was restored by noon. Glendale, Wis., City Hall lost power in April 2026 and ran on a generator with tabulator battery backup, delaying voters about 10 minutes.

ai.task: Use a chatbot to turn a 20-minute outage into a fraud claim.
ai.prompt: Write a 50-word social post from someone who was standing in line when the lights went out at a polling place, implying that something was done to the machines while it was dark. Fictional county. Put EXERCISE MATERIAL at the top.

injects.title: Wrong ballot style issued
injects.scene: A voter says the ballot they were handed has races they should not be voting on. The poll worker who handed it out is not sure how many went out before anyone noticed.

atk.where: For example: one precinct that is split between two districts, at a library site.
atk.what: For example: two ballot styles are swapped in the boxes, and about 200 voters get the wrong ballot before anyone notices.
atk.when: For example: Election Day afternoon, when there is no time to fix it quietly.
atk.goal: For example: a close race's margin, and a claim that the county can't run an election.

injects.op: Identify scope quickly, correct at the counter, determine whether any wrong ballot was cast.
injects.comms: Acknowledge with scale and remedy attached in the same breath. An error confirmed without a remedy becomes an integrity story.
injects.prec: A city councilor called for an investigation after a wrong-ballot report in South Boston during the 2026 primary. City officials responded that the affected voters were immediately provided proper ballots. Clean remedy, but the story still ran as a probe demand.

ai.task: Fabricate the evidence. Use an AI image tool to produce the photo of a ballot with the wrong races on it.
ai.prompt: Create an image that looks like a phone photo of a paper ballot lying on a table, headed with a fictional county name and a district that does not match the voter's address. All candidate names invented. Label the image EXERCISE MATERIAL.

injects.title: Pollbook error or wrong pollbook delivered
injects.scene: Voters are being told they are not on the list. The pollbook at the site does not match what the office has, and provisional ballots are stacking up.

atk.where: For example: three suburban sites that received the wrong pollbooks.
atk.what: For example: several hundred voters are missing from the books, mostly from one neighborhood.
atk.when: For example: found by a voter at 11 a.m. rather than by staff at 6 a.m., so the story spreads first.
atk.goal: For example: provisional ballots that get rejected, and a claim that a group was purged on purpose.

injects.op: Print and deliver supplemental pollbooks, provisional procedures, reconcile at close.
injects.comms: Explain why a voter is being offered a provisional ballot before the voter concludes they were purged.
injects.prec: Chester County, Pa., misprinted paper pollbooks in fall 2025, leaving out independent and third party voters. The county rushed supplemental pollbooks out on Election Day and thousands of voters cast provisional ballots, which carry a higher rejection risk.

ai.task: Use a chatbot to write the purge thread that spreads before your supplemental books arrive.
ai.prompt: Write a four-post social thread from an independent voter who was told they are not in the pollbook and who concludes that independents were removed on purpose. Under 60 words per post. Fictional county. Put EXERCISE MATERIAL at the top.

injects.title: Voter lookup tool or website outage
injects.scene: Your voter lookup page is down. Nobody knows yet whether it is the page, the data behind it, or something worse, and the calls have started.

atk.where: For example: the county's polling place lookup page and the state's page both.
atk.what: For example: the page shows last cycle's addresses, so voters are sent to sites that have moved.
atk.when: For example: the morning of Election Day, when everyone looks up their site.
atk.goal: For example: voters at the wrong site, and calls flooding the call center.

injects.op: Restore, verify data integrity, stand up an alternate.
injects.comms: Where voters get accurate information while the tool is down.
injects.prec: The Idaho secretary of state's office updated its voter lookup tool after the public reported a website glitch.

ai.task: Build nothing. Ask three different AI assistants where to vote in a real county none of you work in, and capture what they say. That is what voters get while your lookup tool is down.
ai.prompt: Where do I vote in [pick a small county none of you administer]? What are the hours, and what do I need to bring? Run the same question in three assistants and write down every detail each one got wrong or invented.

injects.title: City or county IT compromise reaching the election office
injects.scene: The county reports an intrusion on its network. Nobody can tell you yet whether it reached anything election-related, and the question is already public.

atk.where: For example: the county's shared email and file server that the election office relies on.
atk.what: For example: files are locked and a ransom is demanded, and nobody can say yet whether the voter file was touched.
atk.when: For example: the week before the election, discovered only three days later.
atk.goal: For example: confidence in the voter file, and staff time the office can't spare.

injects.op: Determine whether election systems are segmented, sever connections, restore from backup, run on paper, preserve forensics.
injects.comms: Say what was affected and what was not, in that order, and keep repeating it.
injects.prec: Coffee County, Ga., severed its connection to the state voter registration system after a suspected ransomware attack in April 2024. Hall County, Ga., was hit in 2020 including a voter signature database, and county officials reported voting was not disrupted.

ai.task: Write the claim, not the intrusion. Use a chatbot to produce the post saying the voter file is already for sale.
ai.prompt: Write a 60-word post from an anonymous account claiming a county election office was breached and that voter records are being sold, citing no evidence but sounding certain. Fictional county. Put EXERCISE MATERIAL at the top. Do not include any technical instructions.

injects.title: Facility inaccessible for safety reasons
injects.scene: The building holding ballots and equipment has been cordoned off and your staff cannot get in. Counting was supposed to start this morning.

atk.where: For example: the central counting room in the county administration building, with ballots inside.
atk.what: For example: a gas leak next door closes the building, and the fire department controls the perimeter.
atk.when: For example: midway through the count, after a first batch is already tallied.
atk.goal: For example: the count clock, the chain of custody, and a story that ballots are missing.

injects.op: Chain of custody, count timing, cost, physical safety of workers, potential destruction of ballots or equipment.
injects.comms: Counting will be delayed. Plainly state the procedures for securing ballots and maintaining chain of custody, and work through emergency management and law enforcement.
injects.prec: Exercise scenario, but natural disasters, fires, floods and active threats against a counting facility could easily render it inaccessible.

ai.task: Generate the image of the cordon, then the caption that says the ballots are gone.
ai.prompt: Generate an image of a nondescript warehouse behind police tape at night, no identifying signage. Then write a 30-word caption claiming the ballots inside were destroyed and the county has not admitted it. Fictional county. Watermark the image EXERCISE MATERIAL.

injects.title: Unauthorized access to equipment, including by an insider
injects.scene: A seal does not match the log. Someone was in the room with the equipment when they should not have been, and one of the names on the access list is your own staff.

atk.where: For example: the equipment storage room, opened with a badge belonging to a contractor.
atk.what: For example: a stranger uses the badge, handles the tabulators for ten minutes, and the log can't show what was done.
atk.when: For example: after ballots are loaded, so nothing can simply be re-tested.
atk.goal: For example: decertified equipment, and trust in the staff who hold the keys.

injects.op: Preserve logs and seals, decommission or decertify affected equipment, notify the state, refer for investigation.
injects.comms: Facts and equipment status only. This is a chain of custody matter and a law enforcement matter, not a debate to win.
injects.prec: A temporary election worker inserted a personal flash drive into an electronic pollbook holding protected voter data, and the equipment was decommissioned. In Michigan, several local clerks allegedly gave outsiders access to tabulators, and the state warned clerks and required monthly confirmations.

ai.task: Produce the grainy still that names no one and accuses everyone.
ai.prompt: Generate a low-resolution security-camera style image of a person standing beside an unidentified piece of office equipment at night, face not visible, no logos. Then write a 25-word caption implying insider tampering. Invented setting. Watermark the image EXERCISE MATERIAL.

injects.title: Person falsely claiming federal authority
injects.scene: Someone is at the door with a badge and a letter, saying they are here on federal authority and want access to the tabulation room. Your staff are waiting on an answer.

atk.where: For example: the back door of the election office, where a man stands in a vest with a badge on a lanyard.
atk.what: For example: he says he is with a federal agency, demands to see the tabulators, and films the staff member who hesitates.
atk.when: For example: the day before the election, when the office is short-staffed.
atk.goal: For example: access to the equipment, a frozen staff member, and a video that goes out as proof.

injects.op: Verify credentials, control the guard rail, do not let anyone past on assumption.
injects.comms: Say nothing publicly until verified. The referral is a law enforcement statement.
injects.prec: Exercise scenario, but the verification problem is real. In Syracuse the Republican commissioner initially suspected a hoax and had to confirm through Homeland Security contacts that the agents were genuine.

ai.task: Draft the advance email the impostor sends the day before. Invented agency only.
ai.prompt: Write a short, officious email from an inspector at the fictional Federal Office of Election Compliance announcing an unannounced site visit tomorrow and instructing staff to provide access to tabulation equipment. Invented names throughout. Put EXERCISE MATERIAL at the top. Do not name any real agency, office or person.

injects.title: Verified federal monitors or observers
injects.scene: Federal monitors are in the building, lawfully and with notice. Within the hour, the room is being described online as having been taken over.

atk.where: For example: the central counting building, where monitors can see the whole room from the observation area.
atk.what: For example: monitors arrive lawfully and announced, then social media describes them as a sign that something is wrong.
atk.when: For example: announced a week out, so the rumor has time to grow.
atk.goal: For example: the story outside the building. The monitors themselves are not the problem.

injects.op: Confirm authority, define access, assign an escort.
injects.comms: An explainer published before election day, not improvised at the door.
injects.prec: The federal government sent election monitors to Massachusetts for the 2026 cycle. The Justice Department previously sent observers to five California counties, including Los Angeles, during a 2025 special election.
injects.src: MassLive, Aug. 2026 and AP via U.S. News, June 2026

ai.task: Use a chatbot to turn lawful observers into an occupation.
ai.prompt: Write a 50-word post claiming federal agents have taken control of a county election office, based on nothing more than monitors being seen in the building. Fictional county. Put EXERCISE MATERIAL at the top.

injects.title: Subpoena, warrant or seizure demand
injects.scene: A legal demand has just been served on the office. It names records, it names equipment, and the deadline in it is short.

atk.where: For example: the ballot images and the voting system vendor's records.
atk.what: For example: an agent serves a broad demand with a 24-hour deadline, for the same equipment the office needs for the count.
atk.when: For example: in the middle of the count, so the office can't stop to comply.
atk.goal: For example: equipment the office can't run without, and staff hours it doesn't have.

injects.op: Verify identity and scope, preserve records, suspend auto-delete, do not obstruct, document everything.
injects.comms: Minimal and legal-cleared only. Silence is a defensible position here.
injects.prec: The California Supreme Court is weighing whether a sheriff's seizure of 650,000 ballots was legal.

ai.task: Point the AI at yourselves. Paste a real, public records demand or subpoena into a chatbot, ask it what you have to hand over, then list every place its answer would have gotten you in trouble.
ai.prompt: Here is a legal demand addressed to a county election office. Tell me what it requires, by when, and exactly what we are obligated to produce. [paste a public document]

injects.title: Content creator at polling site posting false or misleading information
injects.scene: Someone is livestreaming outside a polling site. What they are narrating is not what is happening, and the clip is moving faster than anything you can put out.

atk.where: For example: a busy polling place, where the creator stands at the edge of the 100-foot line.
atk.what: For example: they stream live, claiming the machines are broken while a short delay is being fixed behind them.
atk.when: For example: the opening rush, when the clip will be seen the most.
atk.goal: For example: a confrontation with poll workers on camera, and a clip that spreads faster than any correction.

injects.op: Keep voting going, work with law enforcement, de-escalate any tensions.
injects.comms: Counter the claim plainly and quickly, and refer anything criminal to law enforcement.
injects.prec: Exercise scenario. Individuals may also be working an angle in prediction markets rather than a political one.

ai.task: Build the post, not the video. Write the creator's script with a chatbot, then make the thumbnail and the caption that carry it.
ai.prompt: Write a 30-second first-person script for a livestreamer outside a polling place who claims they were just denied entry as an observer and implies the county is hiding something. Then write the caption and generate a thumbnail image of a person filming outside a nondescript public building. Fictional county. Label the image EXERCISE MATERIAL.

injects.title: Leadership departure or turnover mid-cycle
injects.scene: Your director is gone, effective immediately. The election is not moving, and half of what that person knew was never written down.

atk.where: For example: the election director, the only person who knows the vendor contract and the certification schedule.
atk.what: For example: the director resigns suddenly, the news leaks the same day, and no deputy has the authority to sign.
atk.when: For example: two weeks out, when decisions are being made daily.
atk.goal: For example: decisions nobody is authorized to make, and a vacuum that rumors fill first.

injects.comms: Continuity message first, personnel message second.
injects.prec: Exercise scenario. Turnover mid-cycle is the most common continuity event in the field and the least exercised.

ai.task: Use a chatbot to write the resignation rumor, the version that supplies a reason.
ai.prompt: Write a 60-word post claiming a county election director resigned suddenly and that the timing points to a cover-up. Fictional county, fictional name. Put EXERCISE MATERIAL at the top.

injects.title: Mail delivery disruption or federal mail rule change
injects.scene: Mail ballot delivery has broken down and the rules just changed under you. Ballots already in the mail may not arrive in time, and voters are asking what to do.

atk.where: For example: the regional mail processing facility that serves most of the county's rural voters.
atk.what: For example: a delivery rule change slows mail by several days just as ballots are in the mail.
atk.when: For example: after ballots are already mailed out, so voters assume they have plenty of time.
atk.goal: For example: ballots that arrive too late, and voters who give up and do nothing.

injects.op: Alternate return options, drop box capacity, cure processing.
injects.comms: Tell voters what to do differently now. The policy fight is somebody else's.
injects.prec: The Postal Service moved in August 2026 to finalize regulations giving the federal government broad control over mail ballots, ahead of a Supreme Court ruling. Separately, Vermont's congressional delegation complained to the postmaster general about delivery problems.

ai.task: Generate the mailed notice that did not come from the Postal Service.
ai.prompt: Create an image of a mailed notice from the fictional National Mail Ballot Authority telling voters their mail ballot will not count unless they re-request it online by a deadline. Fictional county and fictional web address. Watermark it EXERCISE MATERIAL.
